interview.q: What four layers does the CSS box model stack around an element's content?
interview.answer: Content, padding, border and margin, from inside out; the background paints through content and padding but stops at the border.

interview.q: Why does a box with padding and border look wider than its declared width by default?
interview.answer: The default content-box sizing adds padding and border on top of the declared width, so the rendered box is wider than the number you wrote.

interview.q: What does box-sizing: border-box change?
interview.answer: It makes width and height include padding and border, so the declared size is the size the box actually occupies.

interview.q: Which box-sizing value should a global reset usually choose?
interview.answer: border-box, because it makes percentage and pixel widths predictable when padding and borders are added.

interview.q: How is the margin of a block element different from its padding?
interview.answer: Padding is inside the border and carries the background; margin is outside the border and is always transparent.

interview.q: What is margin collapsing?
interview.answer: Adjacent vertical margins of block elements merge into a single margin whose size is the larger of the two.

interview.q: When do margins not collapse?
interview.answer: They do not collapse when a parent has padding or a border, when elements are floated, positioned, flex or grid items, or when overflow creates a block formatting context.

interview.q: What is a block formatting context?
interview.answer: A region of layout in which block boxes are laid out independently, so floats and margins cannot leak across its boundary.

interview.q: How do you create a block formatting context?
interview.answer: Use overflow other than visible, display flow-root, or a flex or grid container; flow-root is the modern, side-effect-free choice.

interview.q: What is the difference between width and max-width?
interview.answer: width sets a fixed size, while max-width caps the size but still lets the box shrink when the container is smaller.

interview.q: Why use max-width: 100% on images?
interview.answer: It keeps an image from overflowing its container while still allowing it to shrink to fit narrow viewports.

interview.q: What does min-width do to a flex item?
interview.answer: It sets a floor below which the item cannot shrink, which often causes overflow if the container is too small.

interview.q: What is the initial value of box-sizing?
interview.answer: content-box, which is why padding and border are added outside the declared width unless you override it.

interview.q: How does padding affect an inline element?
interview.answer: Vertical padding on an inline element paints but does not push other lines apart; horizontal padding does affect spacing.

interview.q: What is the difference between outline and border for layout?
interview.answer: A border participates in box sizing and layout; an outline is drawn outside the border and never affects layout or box size.

interview.q: Why might overflow: hidden clip content unexpectedly?
interview.answer: It clips anything that extends beyond the padding box, including absolutely positioned descendants and box shadows.

interview.q: What does overflow: auto do?
interview.answer: It shows scrollbars only when content overflows, instead of always or never.

interview.q: What is scroll chaining?
interview.answer: When a nested scroll container reaches its limit, the scroll event propagates to the parent, which then scrolls.

interview.q: How do you prevent scroll chaining?
interview.answer: Apply overscroll-behavior: contain to the inner scroll container so it traps the scroll gesture.

interview.q: How does box-sizing affect margin calculations?
interview.answer: It does not; margins are always added outside the box regardless of box-sizing.

interview.q: How is the containing block for a fixed element determined?
interview.answer: Usually the viewport, unless an ancestor has a transform, filter or perspective, which then becomes the containing block.

interview.q: What does z-index actually compare?
interview.answer: It compares stacking levels only among elements that share the same stacking context and are positioned or otherwise eligible.

interview.q: Why might a high z-index not bring an element to the front?
interview.answer: Because z-index is scoped to the stacking context of its ancestor; a parent with a lower stacking context traps it.

interview.q: What is the difference between content-box and border-box for padding?
interview.answer: content-box adds padding outside the declared width; border-box includes it.

interview.q: How does margin: auto center a block horizontally?
interview.answer: It splits the leftover horizontal space equally between the left and right margins of a block with a defined width.

interview.q: Why does margin: auto not center vertically in normal flow?
interview.answer: Vertical auto margins resolve to zero in normal flow; vertical centering needs flexbox, grid or absolute positioning.

interview.q: What is the difference between em and rem in spacing?
interview.answer: em is relative to the element's own font size, so nested padding compounds; rem is relative to the root, so it stays consistent.

interview.q: Why might em-based padding grow unexpectedly?
interview.answer: Because an em on padding resolves against the element's computed font size, which can be larger than the parent's.

interview.q: Why does vertical percentage padding depend on width?
interview.answer: The specification resolves all percentage padding against the containing block's width, including top and bottom.

interview.q: Why is percentage-based vertical padding useful for aspect ratios?
interview.answer: Because padding-top or padding-bottom as a percentage of width creates a box whose height tracks its width.

interview.q: What is the aspect-ratio property?
interview.answer: It sets a preferred width-to-height ratio so the browser can reserve space before the content loads.

interview.q: How do you make a square with CSS?
interview.answer: Set aspect-ratio: 1 / 1, or use padding-bottom: 100% on a relatively positioned wrapper.

interview.q: What is the difference between display: none and visibility: hidden?
interview.answer: display: none removes the element from layout; visibility: hidden keeps its space but hides its rendering.

interview.q: Why might a hidden element still affect layout?
interview.answer: visibility: hidden keeps the box in the flow, so siblings do not move; only display: none frees the space.

interview.q: What is the initial containing block?
interview.answer: The rectangle based on the viewport for continuous media, used when no positioned ancestor exists.

interview.q: How does position: sticky decide when to stick?
interview.answer: It behaves like relative until the scroll position crosses the specified inset, then sticks within its containing block.

interview.q: What happens to margins when a parent has overflow: hidden?
interview.answer: The parent establishes a block formatting context, so child margins no longer collapse with the parent's.

interview.q: What is the difference between min-content and max-content?
interview.answer: min-content is the smallest size the content can take without overflow; max-content is the size if no soft wrapping occurs.

interview.q: When would you use fit-content?
interview.answer: When you want a box to size to its content but never exceed a given maximum, like fit-content(300px).

interview.q: What does the box-decoration-break property control?
interview.answer: It decides whether borders, padding and backgrounds are applied per fragment or across the whole element when it breaks across lines or pages.

interview.q: Why might a box shadow be clipped by overflow: hidden?
interview.answer: The shadow paints outside the padding box, so an ancestor with overflow: hidden clips it unless you add padding or change overflow.

interview.q: What is the difference between margin and gap?
interview.answer: Margin pushes individual boxes apart and can collapse; gap adds space only between items in flex or grid containers and never collapses.

interview.q: How does gap behave in a single-column flex layout?
interview.answer: It adds vertical space between flex items without affecting the outer edges of the container.

interview.q: What is the effect of box-sizing on replaced elements like images?
interview.answer: It still applies, but the intrinsic size and aspect ratio of the replaced content may override the declared dimensions.

interview.q: Why should you avoid negative margins for layout in modern CSS?
interview.answer: They can pull elements out of flow and break stacking and spacing; flexbox and grid gap are clearer and safer.
